title: Corrected active-operation criterion for operadic localization
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Use the ordinary and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $f:M\to O$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads with $O$ ordinary. Assume $M_{[0]}$ and $O_{[1]}$ are spaces and $f_{[1]}:M_{[1]}\to O_{[1]}$ is an equivalence. A map over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is active when its opposite order map preserves the two endpoints. For a color $x\in M_{[1]}$, define $\operatorname{Op}_M(x)$ as follows: its objects are active maps $a:m\to x$; its morphisms are coherent commutative triangles between such maps whose source-change edge is an equivalence in $M$ lying over an identity of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. Include all higher simplices of these data, and define $\operatorname{Op}_O(fx)$ in the same way. These are spaces (arity cannot change). If every induced map $\operatorname{Op}_M(x)\to\operatorname{Op}_O(fx)$ is an equivalence, then for every ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operad $P$ restriction gives a natural equivalence of infinity categories
$$\operatorname{Alg}_O(P)\simeq\operatorname{Alg}_M(P).$$
In particular $f$ has the universal property of an ordinary operadic replacement, at the level of mapping spaces as well as coherent algebra transformations. The hypothesis is about these fixed-arity spaces of operations, not the slice with arbitrary active source-change arrows.
